name: cold_open
text: Sixty-one goals. A league title. A cup final hat-trick. The European Golden Shoe. That is Harry Kane's season. Now here is Lamine Yamal's World Cup. One goal. Zero assists. Eight matches. And the bookmakers have looked at those numbers and made their choice. Harry Kane is the favourite to win the Ballon d'Or. I think they are wrong. And honestly? I don't think it's even close.

name: the_rules
text: Start with what this award actually is. It is not the Golden Boot. It is not a spreadsheet. France Football gives its jury three criteria. Individual performance. Collective performance and titles. And class. A season is judged from August twenty twenty-five to the World Cup final in July. So the question is not who scored the most. It's this. Who was the best player in the biggest moments of the season? Ask that question, and the answer changes.

name: exhibit_a
text: Exhibit A. La Liga. Sixteen goals. Eleven assists. More assists than anyone in the division. A share of the Zarra trophy as the top Spanish scorer. His first senior hat-trick, against Villarreal, in February. And at the end of it, Barcelona were champions, and Lamine was named La Liga's Player of the Season. At eighteen. But the numbers still undersell him. Because every week, the opponent's plan starts with one question. How do we stop him? Double him, and Raphinha is free. Sit off him, and he curls it into the far corner. Press him, and he plays through you. Kane finishes moves. Yamal decides where the move goes.

name: the_gravity
text: There's a word analysts use for this. Gravity. Some players pull defenders towards them just by standing on the touchline. Lamine might have the strongest pull in world football. Watch the full-back. Then watch the winger tuck in to help. Then watch the midfielder drift across, just in case. Three players, all thinking about one teenager. Which means somewhere else on the pitch, someone in a Barcelona shirt has time. That is where a lot of those Barcelona goals really started. It doesn't show up in his goal column. It shows up in everybody else's.

name: exhibit_b
text: Exhibit B. The World Cup. And yes, let's deal with it. One goal, against Saudi Arabia. Then four straight games without a goal or an assist. People were asking whether he should even start the semi-final. But watch the quarter-final against Belgium. No goal. No assist. And he was still named player of the match. Because Belgium spent ninety minutes shifting their whole defence towards one side of the pitch, and Spain played through the space that left. Then France, two-nil. Then the final. Spain one, Argentina nil, after extra time. Argentina managed two shots in the entire game. Two. Spain did not win the World Cup because Lamine scored. They won it because nobody could leave him alone.

name: the_kane_case
text: Now, Harry Kane deserves real respect here. Thirty-six league goals. Fourteen in the Champions League. A hat-trick in the cup final. That is an outstanding season, and if this were the Golden Boot, we would be done. But look at where it ended. Bayern went out of the Champions League in the semi-finals. England led Argentina in the World Cup semi-final, and lost two-one. In the two games that would have defined his year, Kane went home. Yamal went to the final. And he won it.

name: the_others
text: What about the rest? Kylian Mbappé won the World Cup Golden Boot with ten goals. Brilliant. But Real Madrid won nothing, and France went out to Spain. And Ousmane Dembélé? He already has one. PSG won the Champions League again, but they were already the champions of Europe last year. Nobody else has La Liga, the Player of the Season award, and a World Cup winner's medal. Nobody.

name: the_verdict
text: So here is the verdict. Kane had the better numbers. Mbappé had the better tournament for goals. But Lamine Yamal was the best player on the best team in Spain, and an undroppable starter for the champions of the world. And he did all of it as a teenager. He is nineteen. Win this, and he becomes the youngest Ballon d'Or winner in history. The votes are already in. On the twenty-sixth of October in London, we find out if the jury watched the same season we did. Because if they did, this race isn't even close. Tell me in the comments who you would vote for. And if you think I'm wrong, tell me that too.
